questions.q: What does denormalization mean in the context of this lesson?
options: Deleting redundant fields from an object
Deliberately duplicating or pre-calculating data for speed or convenience, at the cost of having to keep the copies in sync
Converting a lookup relationship into a master-detail relationship
Removing all picklist fields from a data model
questions.explain: The lesson defines denormalization as the deliberate choice to duplicate or pre-calculate data for speed or convenience, which creates an ongoing responsibility to keep that duplicated value in sync.

questions.q: Which four calculation types does a native Salesforce roll-up summary field support?
options: SUM, AVERAGE, MEDIAN, and COUNT
COUNT, SUM, MIN, and MAX
SUM, COUNT, and two custom formulas
MIN, MAX, and two percentile functions
questions.explain: Per Salesforce Help, roll-up summary fields support exactly COUNT, SUM, MIN, and MAX -- there is no native AVERAGE option.

questions.q: Per Salesforce Help, roughly how long can it take for a roll-up summary field's value to recalculate?
options: It is always instantaneous
Up to 30 minutes, depending on the number of records affected and other factors
Exactly 24 hours
Recalculation never happens automatically
questions.explain: Salesforce Help states that calculating roll-up summary field values can take up to 30 minutes depending on the number of affected records and other factors.

questions.q: A relationship is correctly modeled as a lookup (for independence reasons), but the business wants an automatically maintained count of related child records on the parent. What does this lesson recommend?
options: This is impossible in Salesforce under any circumstances
Convert the relationship to master-detail regardless of the independence requirement
Build custom automation (Flow or Apex) to denormalize the value, since roll-up summary fields don't exist on lookup relationships
Use a roll-up summary field directly on the lookup relationship
questions.explain: Roll-up summary fields are master-detail-only; when a lookup is the correct relationship type, the lesson recommends declarative automation or Apex to maintain the denormalized value instead.

questions.q: Why does adding a roll-up summary field to a master-detail relationship make a later change to that relationship harder?
options: It has no effect on future relationship changes
Once a roll-up summary field exists on an object, that master-detail relationship can no longer be converted to a lookup
It automatically converts the relationship to a lookup
It deletes the master-detail relationship entirely
questions.explain: The lesson states that once a roll-up summary field is added, the master-detail relationship can no longer be converted to a lookup -- connecting directly back to Lesson 4's point about relationship-type decisions becoming hard to reverse.
